conviction_note: abs_move 10 (event-implied 11.3% off a 25%-spread chain, cut slightly because Q3 comps were guided ten of thirteen weeks into the quarter) with p_up 53: comps are guided and tracking inside the guide, and true-float short crowding into a washed-out IPO points up; macro deterioration after the 9 Sep guide, the +9.7 put skew and the Blackstone margin-loan overhang point down. The findings sum to +0.6 and the scaled number is also +0.6. They match by coincidence: neither was fitted to the other.
bar: Company guide from the 9 Sep 2026 Q2 release: Q3 same-store sales +3.0% to +4.0%, Q3 adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 13%; FY26 same-store sales +2.5% to +3.0%, net unit growth of at least 8%, adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000212704326000008/q22026earningsrelease.htm). The EPS consensus is disputed: Benzinga shows $0.08 and Stocktwits $0.15, and both carry a revenue figure ($208.6M) equal to Q2's actual, so it is probably mislabelled. Every EPS-dependent size is therefore capped small; the same-store-sales and EBITDA bars are company-sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest 11,184,307 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement (FINRA published 10-26), down 10.6% from 12.51M on 9-30, which was up from 2.90M on 7-31. Days to cover 3.7. Aggregators report 3.5% of float, but they divide by about 317.6M fully exchanged shares (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/JMKE/short-interest/). The freely traded float is far smaller: Blackstone affiliates pledged 127.6M of the roughly 233.4M Class A shares (8-K, 2026-09-22) and ADIA holds 35.7M (13G, event date 2026-09-30), which leaves about 70M Class A shares (my inference), including the 46.05M IPO plus over-allotment shares. On that basis the short is about 16-24% of tradeable shares. Skew is +9.69 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest 0.35, ATM spread 25.5% of mid. Equibles reports 6 insider buyers and no sellers over 90 days (net +$1.0M).

findings.finding: Q3 same-store sales were guided at +3.0% to +4.0% on 9 Sep 2026, about ten of the quarter's thirteen weeks in (Q2 ended 28 Jun, so Q3 ended about 27 Sep). The release said the acceleration from Q1 +1.7% to Q2 +2.3%, which was transaction-led, 'has continued into the third quarter', and a call summary has the quarter-to-date run above 3%. The reported comp is therefore close to pre-determined inside the guide, with a lean to the middle or upper half; the bar is the 3.5% midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print as a public company. Q2 comps of +2.3% (accelerating, transaction-led) were bought +7.44% on the day, 9 Sep, then fully retraced within about three weeks to a 30% drawdown. The baseline history is flagged untrustworthy as a base rate.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, which is why it is sized small: it lands inside the company's own guide. What is not obviously priced is that the stock fell about 30% after a release saying comps were accelerating into Q3. A market that trusted the guide would not have taken the stock 25% below the IPO price with targets cut. In-line or upper-half comps confirm a number the price behaves as if it doubts.
findings.independence: The 'tracking above 3%' quarter-to-date remark is a MarketBeat summary of the same call, not a separate source (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-jersey-mikes-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-09/; when fetched, that URL served a different page). Subway's 729 net US closures in 2025 support continued category share gain (https://www.ktvu.com/news/subway-closes-locations-2025).

findings.finding: The consumer backdrop worsened after the 9 Sep guide was set. Placer.ai's August 2026 index had US dining visits down 2.4% YoY, with gasoline above $4 and food-away-from-home prices up 3.4%. September CPI printed 3.7% against 3.6% expected, and restaurant stocks fell 3-4% on 14 Oct. Domino's Q3 2026 US comps were +0.3% against +5.2% a year earlier (13 Oct). Fast-casual visits decelerated to +1.9% in Q3 from +2.2% in Q2. This bears on the Q4 implied guide and the FY same-store-sales range of 2.5-3.0% rather than on the locked Q3 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No guidance change yet as a public company: on 9 Sep the FY comp range was maintained and the stock rose 7.4%. Peers: Domino's fell about 3% pre-market on its comp slowdown (https://finviz.com/news/401785/dominos-pizza-beats-third-quarter-earnings-estimates-but-shares-fall-as-same-store-sales-growth-slows).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector sold off on these prints. The FY guide has not yet been restated against them, and Jersey Mike's has said it is outgrowing industry traffic, so whether the macro reaches its Q4 implied comp is unknown. If the market had fully priced a cut, sell-side targets would have moved below $22 (the lowest is TD Cowen's $22).
findings.independence: This is a macro and peer proxy, not company data, and the company's own Q2 number (comps accelerating while industry traffic fell) argues against it, so it is sized small. The Domino's comp is from Domino's own release, a different source (https://www.franchising.com/news/20261013_dominos_pizza_announces_third_quarter_2026_financial_results.html). Chipotle visits +6.0% (Placer, via NACS) points the other way for one strong brand (https://convenience.org/stay-current/news/2026/october/19/chipotle-is-outpacing-greater-qsr-segment).

findings.finding: The FY adjusted EBITDA guide of at least +20% is back-loaded. Q1 was +50% (to $84M) and Q2 +7% (to $114M, +18% excluding a $10M adverse ad-fund timing hit), so H1 is about +22%. With Q3 guided at 'at least 13%', Q4 has to grow well above 20% to hold the FY floor (my inference; the H2-2025 base is not disclosed). The 10-Q shows a $7M year-to-date ad-fund deficit (advertising expense $115M against revenue $108M) that should reverse, and Area Director buyouts ($52M YTD) mechanically add royalty EBITDA. The FY floor is the line at risk of a trim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 9 Sep reported adjusted EBITDA growth was only 7% and the stock still rose 7.4%. The market accepted the timing explanation that day, then de-rated the stock over the following weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The back-half arithmetic is not in any preview found. Previews quote the guide ranges only, with no Q3 or Q4 EBITDA split, so a trim or a firming of the 20% floor would be new information either way.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release and 10-Q with finding 1. The ad-fund reversal and the trim risk point opposite ways inside one document, so the net is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out. The stock is at $17.26, 25% below the $23 IPO price and 29% below its post-Q2 high. Short interest went from 2.9M shares at IPO to 11.2M on 15 Oct (DTC 3.7), which is roughly 16-24% of the shares that actually trade once Blackstone's pledged 127.6M and ADIA's 35.7M are removed, against 3.5% on the aggregators' fully exchanged base. Meanwhile 21 of 27 analysts rate it Buy with a $27.78 average target, despite target cuts from JPM and Jefferies (29 Sep), TD Cowen to $22 (7 Oct) and Raymond James to $26 (16 Oct).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The single prior print (+7.44%) came with short interest rising from 7.5M to 10.4M over 31 Aug to 15 Sep. A comp acceleration print was bought that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators print 3.5% of float because they divide by the fully exchanged share count, so screens do not flag this as a crowded short. If the true-float crowding were recognised, the skew would not be paying +9.7 vol points for downside on a name whose put/call open interest is 0.35.
findings.independence: Float arithmetic rests on the Blackstone pledge 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000119312526397249/ck0002127043-20260916.htm) and the ADIA 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000110465926118565/primary_doc.xml). Analyst actions are from https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/JMKE/forecast/. This cuts against the +9.69 put skew; sized down for that.

findings.finding: Blackstone affiliates hold about $1.09B of Morgan Stanley margin loans secured on 127.6M Class A shares plus 45.0M Class B shares and units, about 54.3% of the fully exchanged Class A (8-K Items 5.01/8.01, closing 16 Sep, filed 22 Sep). The company agreed not to hinder lender foreclosure. At $17.26 the implied LTV is about 29% (my arithmetic), so this is not a near-term margin call, but it is a standing supply overhang that caps rallies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 4.2% on 21 Sep, the session before the 8-K; it was $20.67 on 15 Sep and $16.86 on 30 Sep.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since the 30% drawdown followed it (Forbes, 25 Oct: 'Blackstone may keep buyers away'). It is filed because it shapes the reaction function: upside on a good print is capped by known supply. Asked what the money buys: it is sponsor liquidity, not company funding, so it is a negative overhang rather than a company-distress signal.
findings.independence: Forbes 2026-10-25 makes the same argument (https://www.forbes.com/sites/jimosman/2026/10/25/jersey-mikes-stock-fell-30-and-blackstone-may-keep-buyers-away/, snippet only). The Boardwalk ML Holdco Form 4 of 2 Oct is a margin-loan holdco transfer, not a sale (accession 0001193125-26-412417).

findings.finding: IPO proceeds of $301M repaid $46M of Series 2026-1 notes and $255M of Series 2026-1A notes on 17 Aug 2026, at a weighted-average rate of about 5.18%. That is roughly $3.9M a quarter of interest saved, and Q3 is the first quarter carrying most of it, which helps the GAAP and adjusted EPS line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: there is no prior EPS reaction to separate from the comp line.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS bar is disputed ($0.08 against $0.15), so it is unclear whether estimates include the paydown; capped small because the bar is unsourced. The company guided Q3 net interest expense at $28M (per Equibles), so it is likely inside guidance.

outside_window.finding: The 180-day IPO lock-up for Blackstone, ADIA and management expires about 2027-01-26 (IPO 30-31 Jul 2026). Per a secondary source; the S-1 was not verified.
An earn-out of up to $250M is payable to pre-IPO holders on the 4,000th store (3,378 at Q2) or on a change in control.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The comp-in-guide and true-float short findings cut against the +9.7 put skew and the 5-day run-up of -3.1%, while the macro and overhang findings agree with them, so p_up sits only 3 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy, and the company's own Q2 number contradicts the proxy direction): finding 2 cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 7 (a sign against a strong skew of +9.69): finding 4 (positioning long) cut from +1.5 to +1.2, kept because the aggregators' float base understates the crowding.
Lesson 6 (disputed EPS bar of $0.08 vs $0.15): finding 6 left capped at +0.2. The lock-up and earn-out are kept in outside_window.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): finding 5 checked; the margin loan is sponsor liquidity, not company funding, and stays a small overhang negative.
Net: the sum is unchanged at +0.6 because the two cuts offset.
